## Refinement Rules (revise in place, do not replace)

The current skill is already a working starting point that needs REFINEMENT, not replacement. Improve it with focused, incremental edits and leave the rest intact.

- Fix the root causes the evidence localizes by revising or extending the responsible guidance; do not append a transcript, a changelog, or a per-instance patch.
- Preserve the working procedure the evidence does not implicate — keep the sections that are already carrying their weight.
- Make targeted, in-place changes: add a missing required step, correct a wrong API/library/pattern, or add an explicit check or pitfall the failing code skipped. A real edit changes what the next solver will DO, not merely how the text reads.
- Cosmetic churn — rewording, reformatting, adding backticks, renaming — accomplishes nothing and is rolled back as a no-op, so do not touch text that is not part of a fix.
- Make the smallest sufficient edit. The caller states the exact effective edit-brake budget, and the system rejects finalized churn above that budget.
